title: Introduce token-cascade stager and saturation-curve emulator for phasewise throughput profiling
author: Asha Mehta
description: Motivation: Our existing benchmark harness runs monolithic saturation ramps that obscure transient hotpath contention and cross-model interference. This PR adds a token-cascade stager: a lightweight runner that issues staged token batches that intentionally vary prefix overlap, interleaving, and KV-cache priming to reveal cascade saturation behavior at sub-second granularity. It also includes a saturation-curve emulator that synthesizes throughput/latency curves for a model+kernel configuration by replaying staged cohorts across concurrency buckets. This helps diagnostics for scheduling, kernel hint selection, and batching heuristics. Changes: - New runner: benchmark/token_cascade_stager.py (config-driven; YAML templates for stage definitions) - Emulator: bench/saturation_curve_emulator.go (parallel probes, per-stage warmup, statistical aggregator) - Reporter: tools/cascade_reporter.ts (CSV + compact JSONL outputs; adds stage metadata and kernel hints) - Test harness updates: bench/harness/runner_integration_test.py and bench/harness/testdata/cascade_examples.yaml - Minor runtime hook: runtime/hints/kern_hint_registry.cc to accept optional stage-derived affinity hints - CI: new perf job config .github/workflows/perf-cascade.yml Checklist: - [x] Stage definition format documented in bench/README.md - [x] Unit tests for YAML parser and reporter - [x] Integration sanity run on small cluster - [x] Perf run with baseline (main) and new runner for comparison Performance notes: Initial runs on c6g-style GPU cluster (8 nodes) produced clear S-curve saturation where models with large KV footprints switch to degraded tail latency at 65-70% token throughput; the cascade stager exposes a microburst window where batching improves p95 but increases p99 for some kernels. See reporter outputs attached as artifacts in CI. Backwards compatibility: Runner is opt-in, harness defaults unchanged. Linear/Jira: ENG-5483 primary ticket, SUP-2241 reproducer. Risks and mitigations: Synthetic stage patterns may not reflect production prompt distribution; we included templating and a corpus of real prefixes to minimize divergence. Follow-ups: integrate stage-derived kernel hints with the scheduler scoring function (ENG-5591).
